label: system-design-junior-vague
questions:
Title: URL shortener
Design a service like a link shortener: users submit a long URL and get a short link that redirects to it.
Scale: 10 million new links a month, 100 times more redirects than new links.

turns.content: Hi! Today we'll design a URL shortener. It's on your screen. Where would you like to start?
I'd start with an API. A POST endpoint that takes the long URL and returns a short code, and a GET on the short code that redirects.
Okay. Before we go further, what are the requirements?
Functional is create and redirect. Non-functional, it should be fast and always available. Reads are way more than writes, like a hundred to one.
How would you generate the short code?
I'd take an auto-increment id from the database and base62 encode it, so seven characters gives billions of codes. Or hash the URL, but then you get collisions.
And where do you store the mapping?
In a database. Maybe Postgres, with the code as the primary key and the long URL.
With a hundred times more redirects, how do you handle the read load?
We just add a cache, like Redis, and it will be fast. And add more servers behind a load balancer.
What gets cached, and what happens when the cache is full?
The popular links I guess. When it's full it would... remove the old ones? I'm not too sure about the details there.
Thanks, that's our time. Good discussion.
